bind.description: Address the HTTP transport listens on, when it is enabled.

enabled.description: Whether the endpoint is listening at all. Off unless configured.

known_drivers.description: Drivers on record, including revoked ones.

public_url.description: Externally reachable URL, for the driver's configuration.

require_token.description:
Whether a bearer token is required. Loopback-only endpoints may disable
it; anything else may not.

client.description:
Client name and version reported by `initialize`, for example
`devin 2.1`. Recorded, not trusted.

connected_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the current connection.

last_seen_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the last request.

name.description: Name the driver gave during the handshake.

peer.description: Peer address, or `stdio` for a local process.

prompt_turns.description: Turns this driver has prompted; the audit trail at a glance.

scopes.description: Scopes actually granted, which may be fewer than requested.

AddProviderRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/providers`.

A provider is inert until it is declared here *and* enabled. There is no
scanning for servers on the loopback interface: a network call is something
the user asked for, not something that happens during startup.

credential_ref.description: Keyring entry to read a bearer token from, for servers that require one.

enabled.description: Whether the provider may be contacted after it is added.

AgentStatus.description: Whether an agent can be used right now.

command.description: Command that will be spawned, for display and debugging.

protocol_version.description: Protocol version reported by the last handshake, when there was one.

AgentTransport.description:
Transport used to drive an agent.

`AcpStdio` is the native path. `Pty` is the program-as-agent adapter, which
lets an ordinary TUI program (freebuff, claude, anything) participate through
a transcript parser. `HttpJsonRpc` is reserved for remote agents.

BridgeTransport.description: Transport a driver is attached over.

CancelAccepted.description:
Response to a cancel request.

`cancelled` is false when the session had no turn in flight: the caller's
intent ("stop") was already true, which is not an error.

cancelled.description: Whether a turn was in flight when the cancel arrived.

turn_id.description: The turn that was running, when one was.

CommitDraft.description:
A generated message the person can edit before anything is committed.

This is a draft: the daemon neither stages nor commits, and the message is not
stored. The transcript of the session that wrote it is the record of how it was
produced.

body.description: Everything after the blank line, empty when there is no body.

breaking.description: Whether the subject marks a breaking change.

emoji.description: The leading gitmoji, when the description starts with one.

message.description: The whole message: subject, a blank line, then the body when there is one.

scope.description: The scope, when the subject names one.

CommitMessageRequest.description: A request to draft a commit message from what is staged.

prompt.description: A template for this request only, instead of the profile's or the default.

session_id.description: The active session whose agent writes the message.

workspace.description: Workspace id, when the client names one. The daemon serves exactly one.

CommitPrompt.description: The effective commit-message prompt, as a client should show it.

template.description: The template before its placeholders are filled.

CommitPromptSource.description: Which prompt a draft would be generated from.

ContextBudget.description: The budget for one run, in tokens except where stated.

max_corpus_bytes.description: Ceiling on corpus text, in bytes, before tokenisation.

reserve_output.description: Tokens held back for the answer.

window.description: Total window to plan against. Defaults to the model's reported value.

used_tokens.description:
Tokens currently in the conversation, including the system prompt and
any corpus that was assembled for the next turn.

window_tokens.description:
The window to measure against. Absent when neither the server nor the
recipe states one; a client must not substitute a default.

ContextStrategy.description: What to do when the assembled prompt would exceed the window.

CorpusSelector.description: One way to pull text out of the workspace into the prompt.

glob.description: Glob relative to the workspace root, for example `docs/**/*.md`.

max_bytes.description: Maximum bytes per file, so one generated lockfile cannot eat the budget.

max_files.description: Maximum number of files to include.

CreateHostRequest.description:
The body of `POST /v1/hosts`.

The kind decides what `address` means: `user@machine` or `machine` for `ssh`,
a distribution name for `wsl`, and nothing for `local`, which is always listed.

address.description: What the transport needs to name it, absent for the local host.

kind.description: How the daemon would reach the host.

CreateRecipeRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/recipes`.

The same fields a recipe file has, without `updated_at`: the file's mtime is
the timestamp, and a client that supplied one would be writing a claim about a
file it does not own.

id.description: Identifier, also the file name under `recipes/`.

notes.description: What this recipe is for, and what it is bad at.

sampling.description: Sampling knobs. Absent means the agent-shaped defaults.

tools.description: Tool ceiling for the promoted agent.

title.description: Optional title; the first prompt supplies one otherwise.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to attach the session to.

CreateTerminalRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/terminals`.

A terminal belongs to a session because that is who owns the work it is doing; a
shell with no session on the daemon's own host would be a second, sessionless way to
run commands there. On a **remote** workspace the work is on that host and sessions
do not run there yet (P8-5), so a client with no session — a browser tab — may ask
for a terminal there without one.

command.description:
Program to run. Defaults to the host's own shell — this machine's, or the
remote host's, because which shell exists is a fact about where it runs.

cwd.description: Directory to start in, relative to the workspace root. Defaults to the root.

oneOf.description:
Session that owns the terminal, when the client has one.

Required for the daemon's own workspace; optional for a workspace on another
host, where a sessionless terminal is the only kind a client without a session
can have.

size.description:
Initial dimensions. Both must be non-zero: a terminal with no columns
cannot display anything, and `vt100` takes `NonZeroU16` for the same reason.

workspace.description:
Workspace to start in, when it is not the one this daemon serves.

A workspace id from `GET /v1/workspaces`. A remote workspace's terminal runs
on that workspace's host — the machine the files are on — through its helper,
while the session that owns the pane is still this daemon's: sessions do not run
on a host yet (P8-5), so the pane is the session's without the workspace being.

CreditStats.description:
Credit balance for one integration.

Amounts are in the provider's own unit — credits, not necessarily currency —
and `currency` carries the label to show. Any field may be absent: some
providers report only a balance, some only usage, and local servers report
neither. [`limit`](Self::limit) is separate because a remaining balance is not
the same as a plan ceiling.

currency.description: What the amounts are counted in, for example `credits` or `USD`.

limit.description:
Plan ceiling for the period, when reported. With `used` this makes the
bar's denominator; without it the bar is indeterminate.

used.description: Credits spent in the current billing period, when reported.

Diagnostic.description:
One problem a language server reported about a file.

Lines and columns are 1-based here, as everywhere else on this wire, and the
columns are counted in characters in [`FileDiagnostics::encoding`] — the daemon
converts the server's own numbers once, where the text is.

code.description: The server's code for it, when there is one.

source.description: Who said it, when the server names itself.

DiagnosticSeverity.description:
How bad a problem a language server reported is.

The protocol's four levels, named rather than numbered: a client that switched on
`2` would be a client that changed meaning when a server did.

DiagnosticsRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/files/diagnostics`.

The path is the question; the text is the version it is about. A buffer edited and
not saved is the text the person is reading, and problems reported about the last
save are problems about a file nobody is looking at.

path.description: The file to ask about, workspace-relative.

text.description: The buffer as the editor holds it. Absent means the file on disk.

workspace.description: Workspace id, when the client names one. The daemon serves exactly one.

DiscoveredModel.description: A model the provider reported, as returned by `GET /v1/models`.

architecture.description: Architecture as reported, for example `llama` or `qwen2_vl`.

capabilities.description: What the model appears able to do.

context_window.description: Context window in tokens, when the server says.

id.description: Model identifier to send in a request.

loaded.description:
Whether the server currently holds it in memory. Absent when the dialect
does not report load state, which is most of them.

model_type.description: Broad class, from the server's typing.

DriverScope.description: What a driver is allowed to do.

ErrorBody.description:
Machine-readable error payload.

`code` is a stable, documented identifier (`invalid_request`, `not_found`,
`conflict`, `permission_denied`, `timeout`, `host_unavailable`,
`model_unavailable`, `agent_failed`, `protocol`, `io`). Clients switch on
`code`; `message` is for humans and may be reworded.

code.description: Stable identifier for the failure class.

details.description: Field-level detail, when the failure is attributable to specific inputs.

field.description: Dotted path of the offending field, for example `preferences.wrap`.

ExtensionContribution.description: One thing an extension provides, named as the profile will see it.

id.description:
Identifier inside that registry, for example `rust-analyzer` or
`night-flight`.

kind.description: Which registry the id lands in.

summary.description: One line of description, so `ext list` is readable without the manifest.

ExtensionDetail.description: One extension, in full, as returned by `GET /v1/extensions/{id}`.

manifest.description: The manifest as written, for reviewing before enabling.

summary.description: The same summary the list endpoint returns.

ExtensionKind.description:
What an extension contributes.

One extension may contribute several kinds; a "Rust pack" is a bundle rather
than a category, which is why this is a list on the summary and a single value
on each contribution.

checksum.description: SHA-256 of the installed directory, verified against the index.

description.description: One sentence, shown in the list.

homepage.description: Project page or repository, for a reader deciding whether to trust it.

publisher.description: Who published it, as the index records them.

FileChange.description:
What happened to a path since the last commit.

One letter per path, not git's two columns: a tree row is a name, and which half
of a change is staged is a question for the source-control pane, which reads the
index and the working tree separately.

FileContent.description: File contents plus the token needed to write them back.

etag.description: Opaque validator; send it back as `if_match` to write.

marks.description:
The lines that differ from the last commit, for a gutter.

With the text rather than behind its own route: a pane opens a file once, and
a gutter that asked a second question about the same file would be a second
round trip whose answer could disagree with the text it is drawn beside. Empty
for a file git does not track, for a workspace that is not a repository, and on
a host with no `git`.

text.description: UTF-8 contents. Binary files are refused rather than mangled.

FileDiagnostics.description:
What a language server says is wrong with a file.

`server` absent means nothing was asked: no server for the language, none
installed, or one that would not start. That is deliberately different from an
empty `items`, which is a server saying the file is clean — a pane that drew both
as "no problems" would be claiming a check that never happened.

oneOf.description: The encoding the columns are counted in, when a server answered.

items.description: The problems, in the server's order.

server.description: The command that answered, when one did.

ignored.description:
Whether an ignore rule hides this entry.

Never true unless the caller asked for hidden rows (`include_ignored` on the
list route): a tree's "show hidden" toggle is the only thing that asks, and
the flag travels with the row because a pane draws a hidden file as a hidden
one rather than pretending it was never ignored.

modified.description: RFC 3339 modification time, when the host reports one.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace root, using `/` as the separator everywhere.

size.description: Size in bytes; zero for directories.

oneOf.description:
How this path differs from the last commit, when it does.

Absent for a clean path, for a workspace that is not a repository, and for a
host with no `git` on it. A tree whose letters are unknowable draws no
letters rather than claiming everything is committed, and the field travels
with the row so a listing is one answer rather than a listing plus a second
question about the same directory.

FileFormat.description:
What a formatter did with a buffer.

`formatted` is true only when a language server answered. A language with no
server, an installed server that refused, or a refusal to start is not a
formatting failure the save has to stop for: `text` is the buffer as it
arrived, and `reason` says why nothing changed. That lets format-on-save be
safe on every file rather than a command that can lose an edit.

formatted.description: Whether a language server answered and its edits were applied.

reason.description: Why the buffer was left alone, when it was.

server.description: The command that formatted, when one did.

text.description: The buffer after formatting, or the input when no formatter answered.

FileFormatRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/files/format`.

The text is the buffer the editor holds, not the file on disk: a save is the
moment the formatter has to see what the person typed. Nothing here writes —
the caller saves the returned text through `PUT /v1/files`.

text.description: The buffer as the editor holds it.

workspace.description: Workspace id, when the client names one. The daemon serves exactly one.

FileRenameRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/files/rename`.

A move is not a write: it changes the name of a file without touching its text,
which is why it carries no `if_match`. The destination is required to be new, so
a rename can never replace a file the caller did not name.

to.description: Its new path, workspace-relative. The destination must not exist.

workspace.description: Workspace id, when the client names one. The daemon serves exactly one.

if_match.description:
The `etag` the caller last read, or absent to create a new file.

A mismatch is a `409`, never a silent overwrite.

workspace.description:
Workspace id, when the client names one.

Absent is the workspace the daemon was started on, which is the only answer
an older client could ask for.

GitChangeKind.description: What happened to a path, on one side of the index.

GitCommit.description: One commit, with enough structure to draw a graph.

authored_at.description: Author timestamp, RFC 3339 with the author's offset.

parents.description: Parent ids, in order. Empty for a root commit.

GitCommitRequest.description:
A request to commit what the index holds.

The message is the whole thing, subject and body, with the blank line between
them: a client that split it into fields would have to put it back together, and
the subject git derives is the first line either way. Nothing here stages.

workspace.description: Workspace id, when the client names one. The daemon serves exactly one.

GitDiff.description:
A unified diff and the files it touches.

The patch is colour-free and external-diff-free, because a person reads it in a
pane rather than in a terminal that would render either. The file list is what a
commit composer iterates without parsing headers.

GitDiffFile.description: One file in a diff, independent of the patch text.

old_path.description: The path before a rename or copy.

path.description: Path after the change, relative to the repository root.

GitHunkRequest.description:
A request to stage one hunk from a path's unstaged diff.

`hunk` is zero-based in the path's **unstaged** diff, not the combined diff
against `HEAD`: the index is the base `git apply --cached` writes to, and a
combined hunk stops describing that base as soon as part of the file is staged.
A client names a hunk; the daemon cuts git's own patch for it and applies that.

hunk.description: The zero-based hunk index in that path's unstaged diff.

path.description: The path whose unstaged hunk should move into the index.

workspace.description: Workspace id, when the client names one. The daemon serves exactly one.

GitIndexRequest.description:
A request to move repository-relative paths across the index or restore them.

The paths are the ones `GET /v1/git/status` reports, so a client never has to
translate a workspace path into the repository's spelling. The answer is the new
status, read after git ran, rather than the request echoed back.

paths.description: Paths relative to the repository root.

workspace.description: Workspace id, when the client names one. The daemon serves exactly one.

GitStatus.description: Branch state and every changed path.

ahead.description: Commits ahead of the upstream. Always on the wire: zero is the answer.

branch.description: Current branch, absent on a detached `HEAD`.

files.description: Every changed path, as git lists them.

head.description: The `HEAD` commit, absent before the first commit.

upstream.description: Upstream branch, when one is configured.

GitStatusEntry.description: One changed path, with the index's answer and the working tree's.

index.description: State in the index: what the next commit would contain.

old_path.description: The path it was renamed or copied from, when it was.

path.description: Path relative to the repository root, with `/` as the separator.

worktree.description: State in the working tree: what the next `git add` would pick up.

GitTreeEntry.description: One path in the working tree, tracked or not.

path.description: Path relative to the repository root, with `/` as the separator.

tracked.description: Whether the index knows about it.

GrepMatch.description:
One line a content search matched.

The line's text travels with the match because a jump list has to be read
before it is chosen from: a list of `src/main.rs:12` is a list nobody can pick
the right row out of without opening every one of them.

line.description: 1-based line number, as an editor counts lines.

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the file the line is in.

text.description: The line as it reads, with trailing whitespace removed.

HostCapabilities.description:
What a host can actually do.

Capabilities are discovered rather than assumed: a host that cannot spawn
processes still edits files, and the UIs need to know that before offering an
agent.

filesystem.description: Can the daemon read and write files here?

lsp.description: Can the daemon run language servers here?

pty.description: Can the daemon allocate a PTY here?

spawn.description: Can the daemon spawn agent processes here?

HostKind.description: How the daemon reaches a host.

oneOf.description: Negotiated capabilities, absent until the host has been reached once.

connected.description: Whether the last connection attempt succeeded.

kind.description: Transport used to reach the host.

activate.description: Activate it in the profile named by `X-Acpilot-Profile` after verifying.

id.description: Identifier from the index, or the manifest's id for a path install.

path.description: Directory to link instead of downloading.

version.description: Version to install. The index's latest when absent.

IntegrationKind.description:
What the stats describe.

Providers and agents share the bar because they share the questions, not
because they share a lifecycle: a provider can serve several agents, and an
agent can outlive the provider that answered its last turn.

IntegrationStats.description:
One integration's stats, as returned by `GET /v1/stats`.

A list of these is what the stats bar renders. Integrations with nothing
reported still appear, with `source: unknown`, so the bar has a stable row
instead of disappearing when a provider is quiet.

oneOf.description:
Context usage, absent when the integration has no conversation attached
(a provider that has not served a turn, for example).

Credit balance, absent for local servers and for plans that do not
expose one.

kind.description: Which kind of integration this is.

label.description: Display label, so a bar can be drawn without a second lookup.

updated_at.description:
RFC 3339 timestamp of the last observation. A stale bar is better than a
silently frozen one, so the age is on the wire.

LineChange.description: What happened to one line since the last commit, for a gutter.

LineMark.description: One marked line, as a gutter counts them.

line.description: 1-based line number in the file as it is now.

LspServerStatus.description: Lifecycle state of a language server.

LspServerSummary.description: A language server as returned by `GET /v1/lsp/servers`.

oneOf.description: Encoding agreed during `initialize`, absent before the handshake.

languages.description: Language identifiers this server is attached to.

round_trip_ms.description:
The last `textDocument/references` round trip, in milliseconds.

The answer and not the index: a cold server's first answer pays for an index
that is paid once, and a figure that mixed the two would make every report
read as slow when only the first question was.

MapArea.description: One part of the workspace, with what it is for and what it depends on.

depends_on.description:
The areas and packages this one leans on, as the agent wrote them.

Names rather than resolved edges: a map is a document, and a dependency the
map gets wrong is a sentence to argue with rather than a build to break.

name.description: What the area is called in a sentence: `TUI shell`, `Daemon`.

path.description:
The directory this area owns, workspace-relative. Empty or `.` is the whole
workspace, which is how a map describes a repository that is not split up.

summary.description:
What the area is for, in the agent's words. One paragraph rather than a list
of files: the tree already lists files.

MetadataSource.description:
Where a fact about a model came from.

The lab is explicit about this because the alternative — a plausible default
context window — silently truncates prompts.

ModeState.description: The modes an agent offers, and the one it is in.

available.description: Every mode the agent advertised, in its own order.

mode.description: The mode in effect once this answer was written.

ModelCapabilities.description: What a model appears able to do, as far as the server admits.

streaming.description: Streams tokens rather than returning one blob.

structured_output.description: Honours a JSON schema for output.

tools.description: Accepts tool definitions and returns tool calls.

ModelCatalogue.description:
One model list, with the providers that could not answer.

The two halves are beside each other on purpose: a list that quietly omitted a
server would look like a server with no models.

models.description: Models from every provider that answered, in provider declaration order.

problems.description: Providers that did not answer, and why.

ModelProblem.description: A provider that could not answer a model list.

ModelRecipe.description: A tuned configuration for one model, as returned by `GET /v1/recipes`.

id.description: Identifier, also the file name under `recipes/`.

notes.description: Free-text note: what this recipe is for, and what it is bad at.

schema_version.description: Schema version, so migrations are explicit.

system_prompt.description:
The master prompt. The whole point of the lab is editing this and seeing
what changes.

tools.description: Tool ceiling for the promoted agent.

updated_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the last edit.

ModelType.description: Broad class of a discovered model, from the server's own typing.

PairDriverRequest.description:
Request the driver sends over the bridge to claim a pair.

Scopes are a request, not a grant: the daemon intersects them with what the
user allowed when the code was issued.

name.description: Name to record for this driver.

requested_scopes.description: Scopes it would like. `answer_permissions` requires an explicit grant.

PairingCode.description:
A one-time pairing code, from `POST /v1/acp/pairings`.

The code is shown in the cockpit and typed into the driver. It is short-lived,
single-use, and useless without the endpoint's token.

code.description: The code to hand to the driver, for example `ALFA-NINER`.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 expiry. Two minutes by default.

handshake_url.description: Where the driver should connect, when the bridge is exposed.

PermissionDecision.description: The decision the broker applied, with its provenance.

PermissionKind.description: What an agent is asking to do.

PermissionOption.description: An answer the caller may give.

PermissionRequest.description: A pending request as returned by `GET /v1/permissions`.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the request was raised.

detail.description: Full detail: the diff, the command line, the tool payload.

options.description: Options the caller may choose from, in display order.

session_id.description: Session that is blocked on this.

title.description: One-line title, safe to show in a notification.

PositionEncoding.description:
Position encoding negotiated with a server.

LSP defaults to UTF-16, while the editor buffers are UTF-8 bytes; the daemon
negotiates explicitly and records what was agreed rather than assuming.

Preferences.description:
Editor and UI preferences, per profile.

Defaults are data (`defaults.toml`), not code: adding a preference should be a
one-line change that every UI picks up, and unknown keys are reported rather
than ignored.

format_on_save.description: Run the formatter on save when one is available.

insert_spaces.description: Insert spaces instead of tab characters.

rulers.description:
Columns to draw a vertical ruler at, in cells.

Rulers are a reading aid, not a hard limit: a line past one is drawn, not
refused. Empty means the editor draws none, which is the default.

schema_version.description: Schema version of this document, so migrations are explicit.

theme.description:
Theme identifier for every surface that does not name its own.

A theme is an extension, so this is the id of one: `acpilot.night-flight`
unless someone says otherwise.

theme_follow_terminal.description:
Solve the terminal's palette from the terminal's own colours.

On, `theme_tui` and `theme` name no theme for the terminal: the background
and foreground the terminal reports (`OSC 11`/`OSC 10`) are the pair a
complete token set is solved around, and they are what the terminal UI draws
with. A terminal that cannot report them falls back to the theme the
settings name, so the key is safe to turn on anywhere.

The desktop app and the browser are unaffected: neither has a terminal to
ask, and a window that took its colours from the shell that launched it would
change appearance depending on where it was started from.

theme_gui.description: Theme for the desktop app, when it should differ from [`Preferences::theme`].

theme_tui.description: Theme for the terminal UI, when it should differ from [`Preferences::theme`].

theme_web.description: Theme for the browser UI, when it should differ from [`Preferences::theme`].

tree_respect_gitignore.description:
Leave paths a `.gitignore` excludes out of the file tree.

On, the tree is the project as git sees it: `target/`, `.venv/` and every
other ignored directory are not rows, which is the difference between a
tree a person can read and a listing of a directory. The daemon answers the
listing, so the matching happens where the ignore files are — a client that
filtered a listing it did not read would be guessing at patterns it has not
seen.

Off, every entry is a row. A workspace that is not a repository has no
`.gitignore` to honour, so the key changes nothing there.

PreferencesPatch.description:
A partial preferences update.

Every field is optional because a patch names only what changed. The daemon
merges the named fields into the profile's `[preferences]` table and leaves
the rest — including keys a newer binary wrote — alone. A full
[`Preferences`] is deliberately not the body: a client that did not know
about a new field must not erase it by sending the object it read back.

format_on_save.description: Run the formatter on save when one is available.

insert_spaces.description: Insert spaces instead of tab characters.

rulers.description: Columns to draw a vertical ruler at, in cells.

theme.description: Theme identifier for every surface that does not name its own.

theme_follow_terminal.description: Solve the terminal's palette from the terminal's own colours.

tree_respect_gitignore.description: Leave paths a `.gitignore` excludes out of the file tree.

ProfileCreate.description: `POST /v1/profiles` — create a profile directory and its registry row.

extends.description: The profile this one inherits settings beneath.

id.description: The directory name and keyring namespace for the new profile.

label.description: Human-readable label; the id when omitted.

ProfileExport.description:
`POST /v1/profiles/{id}/export` — the profile's configuration files.

The document deliberately has no secrets: a keyring reference is exported as
the reference it is, and resolving it is the CLI's opt-in flag, never an HTTP
answer.

files.description: File name to contents, allow-listed to the configuration files a profile owns.

profile.description: The profile the files belong to.

schema_version.description: Schema version of the export document.

ProfilePatch.description:
`PATCH /v1/profiles/{id}` — change the fields a profile's row owns.

Detaching is a separate flag rather than `extends: null`: a nested option is
flattened by serde, so absent and null would arrive as the same value and one
of the two intentions would be lost.

clear_extends.description: Remove the current parent, leaving the profile with no inherited layer.

extends.description: A new parent. Cannot be combined with `clear_extends`.

label.description: Human-readable label; an empty label falls back to the id.

active.description: Whether this is the daemon's currently active profile.

oneOf.description: The profile this one inherits settings beneath, when it does.

workspace_count.description: Number of workspaces opened under this profile.

ProjectMap.description: The workspace map, as `GET /v1/project/map` serves it.

areas.description:
The areas, in the order the agent wrote them.

Always on the wire, empty included: this is the list the answer is about, and
`written: false` is the field that says nobody has written one — a client
should not have to read absence as emptiness as well.

path.description:
Where the map was read from, workspace-relative.

Always the same path today, and on the wire so a client can say where to look
rather than have the location of the file compiled into two places.

updated.description:
When the agent says it wrote the map, as it wrote it.

A string rather than a timestamp for the reason every timestamp on this wire
is: the format should not track a library choice, and the map is the agent's
document rather than the daemon's clock.

written.description:
Whether the file is there at all.

A map nobody has written yet is the normal first state, not an error, so the
answer is an empty map with this false: a panel can say "the agent has not
written one" without a 404 standing in for a sentence.

name.description: Display name; the recipe label is used when absent.

PromotedAgent.description: Result of promoting a recipe: an ordinary agent, plus the caveats.

agent.description: The agent as it will now appear in `GET /v1/agents`.

manifest_path.description: Manifest the entry was written to, so it can be reviewed or reverted.

warnings.description:
Reasons to reconsider: a low tool-call validity rate, a model that the
server has never loaded, a window larger than the host's memory.

PromptAccepted.description:
Response to an accepted prompt.

The turn itself streams over SSE; this only acknowledges that it started.

first_seq.description: Sequence number the client should use as `Last-Event-ID` when reconnecting.

turn_id.description: Identifier for this turn, usable to correlate events and cancels.

PromptRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/prompt`.

`idempotency_key` exists so a retried request cannot start a second turn —
a dropped connection must not cost the user an agent run.

idempotency_key.description: Client-generated key that makes retries safe.

ProviderKind.description:
Which wire dialect a provider speaks.

`LmStudio` reads LM Studio's native `/api/v0` surface, which reports model
metadata (architecture, quantization, `max_context_length`) and per-request
stats such as time to first token. `OpenAiCompatible` is the plain
`/v1/chat/completions` shape shared by Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, OpenRouter and
hosted endpoints — fewer facts, so the UI shows fewer gauges rather than
inventing them.

Anthropic and Gemini are not OpenAI-shaped. They are added as new variants
together with their adapter, never as a guess.

credential_ref.description: Keyring entry holding the bearer token, when the server wants one.

detail.description:
One line of human-readable detail: why it is unreachable, which runtime
answered, and so on. Never a token.

last_probed_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the last probe.

model_count.description: How many models the last probe saw.

RecipePatch.description:
Request body for `PATCH /v1/recipes/{id}`.

Only the fields present move. A recipe id is not editable: the file name is the
identity a run record and an agent manifest refer to.

RecordedRunRequest.description:
The request half of a run record.

This is what the run sent, not what the recipe would send now: the recipe may
have been edited since, and the lab's point is to show the run that happened.

budget.description: The budget the assembly planned against.

corpus.description: Selectors in the order the run used them.

files.description: The files they resolved to, in prompt order.

prompt_sha256.description: `sha256:` and the hex digest of the prompt.

system_prompt_sha256.description: The master prompt's digest, when the recipe had one.

Reference.description:
One use of an identifier, for the references panel.

`column` is a character column rather than a byte offset: a pane places a caret on
the glyph, and a byte column drifts left of it the first time a line holds a `日`.
The line's text travels with the row for the same reason a content search's does —
a list of `src/app.rs:12` cannot be chosen from without opening every one.

column.description: 1-based character column the name starts at.

line.description: 1-based line number, as an editor counts lines.

path.description: Workspace-relative path of the file the use is in.

text.description: The line as it reads, with trailing whitespace removed.

ReferencesRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/files/references`.

The query-string form of the same question, plus the buffer the editor is holding.
A file edited and not saved is the file the person is reading, so the search has
to run over the text that was sent rather than over what the last save left on
disk — otherwise a use typed a moment ago is missing from the list and a use
deleted a moment ago is still in it.

offset.description:
The caret's offset in that file, counted in characters, which is what a server
resolves a name to a symbol with.

Characters rather than bytes because a caret is a glyph: the daemon converts to
the server's own unit, and a byte offset would drift left of the caret the first
time a line held a `日`. Absent means no caret: the text is still the version the
search reads, and no server is asked, because resolving a name needs a place.

path.description: The file the caret is in, workspace-relative.

q.description: The identifier to look for: one word.

text.description:
The buffer as the editor holds it, for the file `path` names.

Sent for the open file only: the rest of the workspace is read where it is,
because a client for a remote daemon does not have it. Sending it is not a
save — nothing here writes — and the daemon never asks for a second copy of a
file it can read.

workspace.description: Workspace id, when the client names one. The daemon serves exactly one.

ResolvedCorpusFile.description:
One file a corpus selector resolved to, as the run recorded it.

Recorded rather than re-derived: the lab shows the files a run actually read,
with their sizes, and a replay must not depend on the workspace still looking
the way it did.

path.description: Path relative to the workspace root, with `/` separators.

tokens.description: Tokens the file was estimated at.

RunPage.description: One page of a recipe's runs, newest first.

oneOf.description: Pass back as `before` for the next page. Absent at the end.

RunRecordView.description: One run's record: what it answered, and what it was asked.

schema_version.description: Schema version of the stored line.

summary.description: The run, as the page also returns it.

corpus.description: Corpus pulled from the current workspace, in order. Absent means none.

idempotency_key.description: Client-generated key that makes retries safe.

corpus_files.description: How many workspace files went into the prompt.

first_token_ms.description: Time to first token, when the transport reports it.

message.description: Error text when the run failed.

params.description: The parameters actually sent, so a run can be reproduced.

stop_reason.description: Why the server stopped: `stop`, `length`, or the server's own reason.

tokens_per_second.description: Throughput, when the server reports it.

warnings.description:
Things that went differently from the recipe: a parameter the server
refused, a truncated corpus, a tool call that had to be repaired.

SamplingParams.description:
Sampling knobs, as the lab presents them.

The set is deliberately small and server-agnostic. An optional parameter the
server *rejects* is retried without and named in `RunSummary::warnings`: a knob
that silently does nothing is worse than no knob. Silent disregard cannot be
observed from outside a sampler, so it is not claimed either.

max_tokens.description: Output cap; `null` means the server's own default.

repeat_penalty.description: Penalty for repeating tokens, where the server supports it.

seed.description: Fixed seed, so a run can be reproduced on the same server and model.

temperature.description: Randomness. Agent work wants this low; drafting wants it higher.

top_k.description: Top-k cutoff, where the server supports it.

SessionEvent.description: One event on a session's stream.

at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the daemon recorded the event.

payload.description:
Kind-specific payload.

A map of unknown values in the document, not a bare `object`: a bare object
is "no properties may be added", and a client generated from that refuses
every payload an adapter actually sends.

seq.description: Monotonic sequence number within the session.

SessionEventKind.description:
The kind of a session event.

This enum is deliberately closed: UIs switch on it exhaustively, and adding a
variant is a wire change that shows up in the OpenAPI snapshot. Adapter-
specific detail belongs in the payload, not in new kinds.

description.description: What the mode changes, when the agent says.

id.description: Identifier the agent uses for this mode.

name.description: Human-readable name shown in a picker.

SessionStatus.description: Where a session is in its lifecycle.

profile.description:
Profile that owns this session.

The daemon routes by profile, so this is normally the profile whose
header selected the router; it is carried so a stored row and a live
summary say the same thing.

title.description: Display title, derived from the first prompt when not set.

updated_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the last event.

mode.description: The id of the mode to switch to, as the agent advertised it.

StatSource.description:
Where one figure came from.

This is recorded per figure rather than per integration: a server may report a
context window but no balance, and a configured plan may name a credit ceiling
the server never mentions.

alive.description: Whether the child process is still running.

command.description: Command that was started, for display.

host.description:
Host the pane runs on, when it is not this daemon's machine.

The id `GET /v1/hosts` lists (`ssh:user@machine`, `wsl:Ubuntu`). A shell whose
bytes come from another host looks exactly like a local one in a picker, which is
why the pane says which it is.

oneOf.description:
Session that owns it, when one does.

Absent for a terminal a client asked for in a remote workspace without a
session: a browser tab on that workspace's shell has none, and sessions do not
run on a host yet (P8-5). A local terminal is always a session's.

workspace.description:
Workspace the pane runs in, when it is not the one this daemon serves.

A pane asked for in a named workspace runs in that tree, which on another host
is a tree this daemon never walked. Absent means the daemon's own workspace: the
one implied by every other route.

ThemeAppearance.description: Light or dark, so a UI can pick the right half of a theme pair.

ThemeSummary.description:
A theme as returned by `GET /v1/themes`.

Themes are the one extension kind every surface consumes, so they get a
first-class route rather than being reachable only through the extension list.

appearance.description: Which half of the day it is for.

built_in.description: `true` for the themes compiled into the binary.

oneOf.description: Extension that provided it, when it did not come from the binary.

TokenUsage.description: Token counts for a run, and whether they are trustworthy.

estimated.description:
`true` when these are the lab's estimate rather than the server's
reported `usage`. The UI must not style them the same way.

ToolExposure.description:
Which tools a model-backed agent may *ask* for.

This is a ceiling, not a grant. Every call still goes through the permission
broker; a tool left out here does not exist as far as the model is concerned,
which is a much better place to enforce a boundary than a prompt.

max_steps.description: Hard cap on model→tool→model steps per turn.

UpdateProviderRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH /v1/providers/{id}`.

An omitted field is unchanged. Changing where the provider lives is a new
question, so the route probes again; changing only a label does not.

enabled.description: Whether the provider may be contacted.

WorkspaceOpenRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/workspaces`.

Opening is idempotent: the same `host_id` + `root` pair resolves to the same
workspace, so a client can call this on every launch.

host_id.description: Host to open the workspace on.

steal.description:
Take the root from the profile that opened it first.

The default is to refuse: two profiles editing one checkout is the
isolation this phase exists to prevent. A client that really means it says
so here, and the daemon records the new owner and logs the transfer.

name.description: Display name, defaulting to the directory's basename.

profile.description:
Profile that owns this workspace.

Two profiles may see the same host path; the owner is what makes one
profile's workspace id unacceptable in another's request.

root.description: Root path, as the host spells it (not translated to the client's platform).

session_count.description: Number of sessions recorded against this workspace.

bearer.description: A TCP listener requires this on every request. The daemon writes the token to a `0600` file in its runtime directory (`token`, beside the socket) and logs the path when it binds. A request over the unix socket needs none: that transport's access control is the filesystem.
